transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-13 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya Singh (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO, Cedar), Marcus Bell (Lead Engineer, Cedar), Priya Rao (SRE, Cedar)

Summary: quick SDK walkthrough focusing on python/typescript quickstarts, auth, env vars, and quick local->staging->prod flow. Went over token handling, KMS note, and private/VPC constraints. Agreed next steps: pricing, repo links, pilot scope, benchmark session.

00:00 - Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
00:03 - Lena: yeah loud and clear, thanks for doing this.
00:06 - Maya: quick intro, I'm Maya Singh, AE for Redwood, with Ethan our SE, we'll walk through the SDK quickstarts for Python and TypeScript and then run a short live demo of auth and environment setup.
00:15 - Ethan: hi all, I'll jump into the code and runtime considerations, expect some notes on batching and KV cache.
00:22 - Marcus: great, we mostly want to see how fast we can get up and running and what the auth setup looks like for our CI/CD.
00:28 - Priya: and security — SSO, KMS, audit logs — that's top for us.
00:33 - Ethan: understood, we'll cover SAML/SSO options and KMS integration — Redwood supports customer-managed keys and HSM integrations, we'll share the security doc.
00:42 - Maya: starting with the python quickstart — repo link in the chat, it's the standard redwood-python SDK. The flow is: pip install redwood-sdk, set REDWOOD_API_KEY or for service tokens set REDWOOD_SERVICE_TOKEN, then redwood.client.generate(...)
01:00 - Lena: is the env var the only way? we prefer to use vaulted secrets in our CI.
01:06 - Ethan: yep env var is just the simplest, but the SDK supports credentials providers. You can configure a file-based creds or integrate with Hashi or AWS Secrets Manager, and we have a small example in the repo.
01:20 - Marcus: when you say service token, is that per-service or per-deployment?
01:25 - Maya: service tokens can be scoped per project or per-pipeline, and you can rotate them. For Dedicated or Private customers we have extra options for mutual TLS and VPC peering.
01:36 - Priya: and audit logs for who used the key?
01:39 - Ethan: yes audit logs are available — token-level logging, request/response metadata retained per your retention settings, and they tie to SSO user identities when applicable.
01:50 - Maya: moving to TypeScript quickstart, npm i @redwood-inference/sdk, same pattern env var REDWOOD_API_KEY or use redwood.config.ts for typed configs. We showed the chat sample and the streaming API example in the quickstart.
02:10 - Marcus: any gotchas with Node runtimes we should know about?
02:13 - Ethan: watch for long-lived connections and streaming; if you're in serverless you might need to reuse connections and the SDK exposes a client reuse pattern. Also be mindful of sequence length and batching to control cost.
02:28 - Lena: can you show the auth flow in the console?
02:30 - Maya: sure — switching to shared screen — console, top right, API keys, you can generate scoped keys, set expiry, restrict to models or routes. For enterprise accounts there is an SAML SSO setup and RBAC so you can map groups to roles.
02:45 - Priya: do you support SCIM for user provisioning?
02:48 - Ethan: yes SCIM support for provisioning is available for enterprise customers, we can include that in the security packet.
02:55 - Maya: quick note on environments: recommended pattern is local dev -> staging with test keys -> prod with rotated service token and KMS-backed keys. We have a sample env config in the repo showing REDWOOD_ENV=staging and REDWOOD_API_KEY pointing to a secrets provider.
03:12 - Marcus: about Dedicated vs Hosted — our compliance team prefers Dedicated but ops wants to keep cost under control. How does pricing change?
03:20 - Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity pricing — monthly commit — tends to lower per-token cost at higher throughput. Hosted is usage-based. We'll send a pricing slide with a few example TCO calculations.
03:33 - Lena: privately hosted in our VPC is non-starter for us unless we can get audited on site, we prefer Redwood Private with VPC peering.
03:40 - Ethan: Redwood Private supports VPC peering and customer-managed networking; we also support air-gapped installs for on-prem. We'll include the Private deployment checklist.
03:52 - Priya: on encryption, do you support CMEK?
03:55 - Ethan: yes customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) via KMS, plus optional HSM. We'll attach the KMS integration guide.
04:05 - Maya: switching back to code — walking through a python snippet — set REDWOOD_API_KEY then from redwood import Client; client = Client(); resp = client.generate(model="rwd-7b", prompt="Summarize ..."). We demoed a short run and showed streaming tokens in the console.
04:30 - (audio glitch)
04:33 - Marcus: sorry, glitch — can you repeat the streaming part?
04:35 - Ethan: sure — streaming uses client.stream(...) and the SDK returns an async iterator in python or an evented stream in node. It's efficient for UI use cases.
04:45 - Lena: how do you handle fallbacks if a model is unavailable?
04:48 - Maya: Smart routing — policy based. You can pin to a model or allow fallback to a compatible variant, with latency and cost routing rules. Good for graceful degradation.
04:59 - Marcus: any observability hooks we can integrate?
05:02 - Ethan: yes we expose metrics (latency, tokens, errors) and there are tracing hooks — you can attach a request id and send logs to Datadog/Prometheus. Console shows per-route token cost breakdown.
05:18 - Priya: let's talk about batching — our throughput is bursty, will batching add latency?
05:22 - Ethan: batching reduces per-token cost but does add micro latency; Redwood Optimize suggests batching configs based on seq length distribution. You can set SLOs so batching doesn't break latency targets.
05:37 - Lena: do you have an example of a CI pipeline step for testing a deployment?
05:40 - Maya: yes — we shared a sample github action in the repo: uses REDWOOD_SERVICE_TOKEN from secrets, runs a quick smoke call to the dev model, and then runs perf checks. We'll share that link.
05:53 - Marcus: any rate limit handling?
05:55 - Ethan: SDK surfaces 429s and retry helpers; you can configure exponential backoff and small client-side queues. For Dedicated customers we can adjust quota limits.
06:08 - Lena: security review — our legal wants SOC2 docs and pen test reports.
06:11 - Maya: we will attach SOC2 reports and the security whitepaper; for private deployments we can do additional audits as part of enterprise onboarding.
06:20 - Priya: logs retention — can we set retention per project?
06:23 - Ethan: yes retention policies are configurable; we also support log forwarding to your SIEM.
06:30 - Maya: quick live demo — I run the python quickstart, show env var set, run the generate call, results return in ~300ms in this demo (local network).
06:45 - Marcus: realistic latencies for your hosted region?
06:48 - Ethan: typical 50-150ms token latencies for rwd-7b in us-west, depends on seq length. We'll provide regional perf numbers in the benchmark doc.
07:00 - Lena: for benchmarking can you run a 10k request synthetic test?
07:03 - Maya: we prefer to run joint benchmarks; we'll schedule with your team and run with your payloads. Marcus will provide traffic patterns.
07:12 - Marcus: okay will export sample payloads and seq length histogram.
07:15 - Priya: for CI/CD can we rotate keys automatically?
07:18 - Ethan: yes you can rotate service tokens via the console or API; we also support short-lived tokens for ephemeral workloads.
07:25 - (15:00 mark)
07:26 - Maya: moving to TypeScript sample — show node quickstart, how to use client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }), and streaming using client.stream. We also discussed client reuse in lambda.
07:42 - Lena: any language-specific differences for embeddings vs chat?
07:45 - Ethan: embeddings are synchronous calls in the SDK but have batching helpers. Chat uses the chat-specific API with messages array. Both have token cost metrics.
07:58 - Marcus: do you store prompts? we need to ensure PII is not retained.\08:02 - Maya: data retention is configurable; by default hosted redwood may retain for debugging but enterprise customers can opt-out or route logs to customer storage. We'll include the data handling policy doc.
08:18 - Priya: about private deployment, is there a minimum commit or minimum node requirement?
08:21 - Ethan: Private has a minimum monthly license and some infra requirements; we'll include the Private deployment sizing guide.
08:32 - Lena: competitive question — how do you compare cost to OpenAI?
08:35 - Maya: varies by model and throughput; Redwood focuses on inference economics — batching, caching, quantization and Dedicated pricing to lower unit costs. We'll include TCO examples.
08:48 - Marcus: ok let's recap next steps.
08:50 - Maya: recap — we'll send pricing and slides (Dedicated vs Hosted), security docs (SOC2, KMS guide), quickstart repos (python & ts), schedule benchmark session, and Marcus to share payloads.
08:59 - Lena: timeline — we want a pilot in January, ideally start 2027-01-10.
09:04 - Maya: noted — we'll aim to have everything to you by 2026-12-15 and pick a benchmark slot for the week of 2026-12-20.
09:12 - Marcus: thanks, good session.
09:14 - Priya: thanks, appreciate the security details.
09:16 - Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and items.
09:20 - (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription artifacts: occasional dropped words, brand names misrecognized (e.g., 'Kubernauts' instead of 'Kubernetes' in auto-transcript), and occasional speaker attribution errors.
